title: Four Ways to Answer the Same Questionnaire
scopeNote: This keeps the response grids, the recoded scores and the balanced-keying control, which the original's own notes call the most practically useful thing in it. Three further styles including random and straight-line responding, the split-half and longest-run statistics and the diagnosis exercise stay in the longer version.
summary: Four fictional respondents with identical true standing use a five-point scale differently. Reverse-worded items rescue one of them almost exactly and do nothing whatever for the other two.
learningObjectives: Recognise acquiescent, extreme and midpoint responding from a response grid.
Explain why reverse-worded items cancel an acquiescent respondent's bias.
Explain why the same recoding does nothing for extreme or midpoint responding.
Explain why an unbalanced scale cannot distinguish agreeing readily from holding a trait strongly.
Say what a response pattern can and cannot establish about a person.
interactionTypes: a prediction about which style balanced keying rescues
a live control over where all four respondents actually stand
a toggle between a balanced and an unbalanced questionnaire
four response grids that regenerate as the controls move
recoded scores shown against the score the true standing implies
a guided setting that removes the reverse wording
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. No questionnaire is administered to the learner and nothing is inferred about them.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout. True standing is a native range input reporting its value in text, and the questionnaire toggle is a button carrying aria-pressed and a visible word saying which version is in use. Every answer is in a real table with row and column headers, and reverse-worded items are marked in the column heading with a letter rather than by colour, so the grid is fully readable without the figure. Each score tile states in words how far the score is from the accurate value and carries a non-colour state signal. The chart labels every respondent by name, puts the values in an aligned column, and the chart description gives all four scores and the accurate value. Nothing is timed and there is no motion.
dataStatus: Four invented respondents whose answers come from a formula, generated from a fixed random seed so the same grids appear every time the page is opened. Nobody was measured.
simulationNotes: An answer is 3 + standing * keying * discrimination + noise, transformed by the respondent's style, rounded and clamped to 1 to 5; reverse-worded answers are recoded to 6 minus the answer before scoring. All four respondents share one noise draw, so the four rows are one underlying set of reactions expressed four ways. Independent draws per respondent would model four people better and demonstrate far worse, because the differences between rows would then be part style and part sampling noise and the cancellation the activity turns on would be buried. The draw is centred within each half of the questionnaire so both halves have mean zero; without that the straightforward respondent, who is the benchmark everything is read against, sits up to a quarter of a point off the score their standing implies, which invites the reader to explain the model's noise as a response style. The result the activity exists to show is arithmetical: acquiescence adds a constant to every answer, and recoding turns that constant into a subtraction of equal size on the reverse-worded half, so a balanced scale cancels it; extreme and midpoint responding multiply the distance from the midpoint, and a multiplication survives the flip unchanged. Balanced, the acquiescent score sits within about a third of a point of the straightforward one; unbalanced, it sits more than a point higher. The cancellation is imperfect at the top and bottom of the scale, where answers clamp and there is no room left for the constant, which is a real property of bounded rating scales and is reported rather than hidden. Simplifications: four styles rather than seven, equal discrimination for every item, and a style as a fixed transformation rather than something that drifts through a questionnaire.
readmeTopic: what reverse-worded items fix, and what they leave exactly as they were
